title: Pax airship disaster
summary: The Pax experimental hydrogen airship exploded at 5:40 a.m. during an untethered flight test over Paris after the pilot struggled to maintain control in windy conditions. The investigating committee attributed the explosion to the design defect of placing the combustion engine too close to the hydrogen envelope, where engine heat or electrical arcing ignited the fuel vapors. Both the Brazilian inventor Severo and his French mechanic were killed when the wreckage fell onto Maine Avenue.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by the proximity of the combustion engine to the balloon's exhaust valve and gas envelope, which allowed ignition of hydrogen when the engine overheated or suffered an electrical short circuit during sustained control inputs in gusty wind.

factors.evidence: engine was only three feet from the hydrogen envelope
flames first erupted from the engine, soon enveloping the entire aircraft
pilot fought to remain in control of the airship for fifteen minutes as the 40 hp engine was not powerful enough in these conditions
had difficulties fighting the wind, making circles of 100 to 150 meters diameter
airship exploded at 5:40 a.m., the balloon unable to withstand the internal pressure

events.text: Pilot resumed untethered flight after fifteen minutes of tethered testing and landing
Flames first erupted from the engine
Fire enveloped the entire aircraft and airship exploded over Maine Avenue
Wreckage fell onto Maine Avenue, nacelle crashed through ceiling of house
